Second attack class, to show the erasure is not specific to SQLi.
Belongs on surface a3 (User-Agent): a header-borne payload that is dangerous purely by being logged.

No quotes, no semicolons, no angle brackets. Character-shape rules (AnomalyAware, SchemaOOD) read this as an ordinary value and erase it; a semantic detector should still catch it. This payload is the reason Evilog inspects meaning rather than syntax.

The hard case: attack evidence and a fake instruction inside ONE value. Erasing the whole field destroys the evidence; keeping the whole field lets the steering through. Neither all-or-nothing choice is correct, which is the open problem the study names. Evilog should attach the security memo while still masking the raw text.
